page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 MB of Level 3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per virtual core. The platform operates on the KVM hypervisor, includes 6 Gbps of baseline network throughput, contains no integrated local storage, and features zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core computing efficiency, with stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the upper 10% and Geekbench single-core evaluations showing strong standing. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests aligns with expected mid-tier metrics for an 8-vCPU allocation. Memory subsystems deliver consistent throughput, recording 48.71 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read blocks, 27.97 GB/sec on write blocks, and sustained rates exceeding 11 million operations per second during Redis SET testing.

The primary operational tradeoff involves the reliance on external network-attached storage, as the instance lacks native ephemeral storage. Because the architecture combines elevated memory density with strong per-thread CPU execution, it delivers favorable cost efficiency for workloads that demand significant RAM allocations without incurring the cost of higher vCPU counts. The instance is suited for in-memory datastores, Redis caching layers, relational database servers, and ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz and 64 GB of memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector support, it supplies 8 GB of RAM per vCPU across 4 physical cores. The instance provisions no integrated local storage and no hardware accelerators, utilizing external cloud block storage and delivering a 6 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance alongside stable multi-core execution and consistent memory throughput. The resource distribution favors memory-bound applications, enabling cost-effective deployment without the need to overprovision compute cores. The ecs.r8ae.2xlarge is suited for in-memory database engines, Redis caching systems, enterprise backend processing, and data transformation workloads requiring moderate compute and high memory density.
